## Executive Summary

This report evaluates historical risk and simulates 5-year forward-looking returns for a multi-asset portfolio. Asset innovations are modeled using a Student's $t$-distribution ($\nu = 5$) to account for leptokurtic behavior and fat-tail crash probabilities observed in financial markets.

## 1. Portfolio Construction & Historical Data

```{r}
#| label: data-setup
library(tidyverse)
library(tidyquant)

weights <- tibble(
  symbol = c("VT", "GLD", "BTC-USD", "SRFM", "ONDS", "BRK-B", "BIL", "GOOGL"), 
  weight = c(0.589, 0.124, 0.023, 0.003, 0.032, 0.055, 0.138, 0.036)
)

portfolio <- tq_get(weights$symbol, from = "2020-01-01", to = "2026-11-10")

returns_data <- portfolio |> 
  group_by(symbol) |> 
  tq_transmute(
    select = adjusted, 
    mutate_fun = periodReturn, 
    period = "daily",
    type = "arithmetic", 
    col_rename = "daily_return"
  ) |> 
  drop_na()

portfolio_returns <- returns_data |> 
  tq_portfolio(
    assets_col = symbol, 
    returns_col = daily_return, 
    weights = weights, 
    col_rename = "portfolio_return"
  )
```

## 2. Downside Risk Analysis (VaR & Expected Shortfall)

Value at Risk (VaR) is calculated empirically at the 95% confidence level ($\alpha = 0.05$), alongside Conditional Value at Risk (Expected Shortfall):

$$\text{ES}_{\alpha} = \mathbb{E}[R \mid R \le \text{VaR}_{\alpha}]$$

```{r}
#| label: var-analysis
var <- quantile(portfolio_returns$portfolio_return, probs = 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

expected_shortfall <- portfolio_returns |> 
  filter(portfolio_return < var) |> 
  summarise(expected_shortfall = mean(portfolio_return))

ggplot(portfolio_returns, aes(x = portfolio_return)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100, aes(fill = portfolio_return > var)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = var, color = "black", linewidth = 1.2, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Daily Portfolio Returns and 5% VaR Threshold",
    x = "Daily Return", 
    y = "Frequency",
    fill = "Exceeds 5% VaR"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 3. Fat-Tailed Monte Carlo Engine

Asset returns typically exhibit excess kurtosis. Random innovations $T_t$ are sampled from a Student's $t$-distribution with $\nu = 5$ degrees of freedom and scaled to maintain portfolio volatility:

$$Z_t = \mu + \sigma \sqrt{\frac{\nu - 2}{\nu}} \cdot T_t, \quad T_t \sim t(\nu)$$

```{r}
#| label: monte-carlo-sim
set.seed(42)

portfolio_stats_return <- portfolio_returns |> 
  summarize(
    mean_return = mean(portfolio_return, na.rm = TRUE), 
    portfolio_sd = sd(portfolio_return, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

nu <- 5
log_mean_return <- log(1 + portfolio_stats_return$mean_return) - ((portfolio_stats_return$portfolio_sd)^2) / 2
log_sd <- portfolio_stats_return$portfolio_sd
scale_t <- log_sd * sqrt((nu - 2) / nu)

# 10,000 simulations over 1,260 trading days (~5 years)
portfolio_simulation <- replicate(
  10000, 
  exp(cumsum(log_mean_return + scale_t * rt(1260, df = nu))) * 28100
)

# Plotting sample trajectories
simulation_sample_tibble <- portfolio_simulation[ , 1:100] |> 
  as_tibble() |> 
  mutate(day = 1:1260) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = -day, names_to = "simulation_no", values_to = "portfolio_value")

ggplot(simulation_sample_tibble, aes(x = day, y = portfolio_value, group = simulation_no)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 28100, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "5-Year Monte Carlo Trajectories (100 Sample Paths)",
    x = "Trading Days", 
    y = "Portfolio Value (£)"
  )
```

## 4. Key Terminal Risk Metrics

```{r}
#| label: terminal-metrics
final_values <- portfolio_simulation[1260, ]
five_year_var <- quantile(final_values, probs = 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
five_year_cvar <- mean(final_values[final_values < five_year_var])
losing_chance <- mean(final_values < 28100)
doubling_chance <- mean(final_values > 56200)

tibble(
  Metric = c("Initial Capital", "5-Year 95% VaR", "5-Year 95% CVaR", "P(Loss at 5 Years)", "P(Doubling Capital)"),
  Value = c(
    "£28,100",
    paste0("£", formatC(five_year_var, format = "f", digits = 2, big.mark = ",")),
    paste0("£", formatC(five_year_cvar, format = "f", digits = 2, big.mark = ",")),
    paste0(round(losing_chance * 100, 2), "%"),
    paste0(round(doubling_chance * 100, 2), "%")
  )
) |> 
  knitr::kable()
```
